# Bugs Found While Building

Real defects hit during development. Each entry: what broke, why, the fix, and the
regression test that now guards it. Opened empty on purpose — an entry is written
when a bug is actually found, never pre-filled.

---

## Bug 1 — `search_providers` returned 2 providers where the contract requires 3–8

**Observed.** `test_search_returns_between_3_and_8_with_required_fields` failed on
the first run: a search for `("plumber", "Indiranagar")` returned 2 providers.

**Cause.** The fixture was generated by iterating 12 providers with
`service = services[i % 3]` and `area = areas[(i // 3) % 3]`. That combination is
not surjective onto the 9 (service, area) pairs — only 6 pairs ever appear, and two
of them get a single provider each. The mock then filtered a 12-row table down to
2 hits. The contract in the assignment says the tool returns 3–8 providers, so the
fixture could not satisfy the interface it was built to imitate.

**Fix.** Generate the fixture per (service, area) pair with 3–6 providers each, 39
rows total, so every legal search returns inside the contract's range. The mock
was not changed: it was correctly returning what the data held.

**Regression test.** `tests/test_mock_tools.py::test_search_returns_between_3_and_8_with_required_fields`.
It asserts the range for one pair; `test_all_pairs_satisfy_contract` extends it to
all nine pairs so a future fixture edit cannot reintroduce a thin pair.

---

## Bug 2 — the classifier refused "sounds good, thanks" as an approval

**Observed.** `test_classify_table` failed on `"sounds good, thanks"`: expected
`affirm`, got `other`. `"yep, go ahead"` failed the same way.

**Cause.** The first implementation matched affirmatives against a set of single
tokens, so every multi-word phrase in `AFFIRM` (`"go ahead"`, `"sounds good"`,
`"book it"`, `"that's right"`) could only ever match if it was the *entire*
normalised reply. A user who answered "sounds good, thanks" — the most natural way
to accept an offer — was silently treated as ambiguous and re-prompted. The
tool-call path was safe (it refuses to approve), but the failure mode is a user
stuck in a confirmation loop saying the same thing more firmly, which the demo
would have hit on the first take.

**Fix.** Two passes. First strip any multi-word affirmative phrase out of the
normalised reply, then require the remaining tokens to be filler words
(`please`, `thanks`, `it`, `then`, …). Single-token affirmatives keep the token-set
path. A reply that still carries a content word outside the filler set remains
`other`, so "go ahead and book the cheaper one" is still not an approval — that
distinction is what stops the loosening from becoming a substring match on "yes".

**Regression test.** `tests/test_classify.py::test_classify_table` now carries 38
cases, including four padded affirmatives that must pass and
`"go ahead and book the cheaper one"` which must still fail. A looser classifier
that reintroduces the substring bug fails that case.
